notes.text: A handwritten working list in three physically distinct groups headed Raynaud, Illusie 1 and Deligne with a doubtful adjacent mark. The title entries are positioned in a right column. It is not a proof or a computation.
Lists a Mumford Theta title with I and II, Papiers Kiehl, and Artin-Winters. The first vowel of the title word and the retraced Artin cluster remain doubtful.

Lists Monsky-Washnitzer I and II, letters and an Affine duality item for Hartshorne, letters to Quillen, infinitesimal extensions, a cancelled Notes item with (pluriel), R. Wood Bourbaki calcul différentiel, Complexe cot with a small lower mark, an Atiyah-extension item with Omega^1, Koszul 2 articles, and cancelled Borel Lecture Notes.

Includes a second Monsky-Washnitzer item, a cancelled Serre item on Vect. Witt and var. abéliennes with a characteristic condition, a Griffiths title beginning “On monodromy”, a cancelled letter entry, a cancelled short start, and cancelled Weil, Artin, Lichtenbaum, Manin and Harder items.

No securely readable verbal hesitation such as peut-être occurs. Source incompletion is explicit in the four terminal marks after “On monodromy” and the two-short-plus-long graphic after Omega^1. The cancelled “Que/Qui” is a short abandoned start. The mark after Deligne may itself be a question mark, but that is unresolved. Reading doubts are editorial and are not presented as authorial hesitations.

No date or overall title is visible. Illusie is followed by 1; the mark after Deligne remains 1/2/?. Roman I and II occur in the first titles. Two entries explicitly say 2 articles. The underlined 13 in the Artin entry is preserved without assigning it a page-count meaning. The lower-left 3 is the archive mark and appears only in a comment.

All textual entries are handwritten. Dark blue/black writing and paler grey strokes are visible; pencil-like is a visual description, not a material identification. No typewriter double striking, script sheaf alphabet or double-struck mathematical alphabet is introduced. The Roman numeral head/foot rules are separately observed.

H is treated as an unverified direct transcription, not an independent authority for expanding Ch., Vect., car or cot. Its list-joining em dashes and semicolons are editorial separators and are excluded from differences. Local ill spans are quoted literally and scoped to the unread source region; nearby ill does not make an otherwise unmarked H word doubtful.

The supplied macros are not redefined. Existing deletion state is retained and literal paths are drawn additionally where source extents, separate strokes, hatching or waviness carry information. In the lower parenthesis, the six schematic diagonals and terminal return reproduce the observed hatch pattern approximately; original pen lifts remain unresolved.

notation.evidence: Closed oval with a distinct transverse median bar in the Mumford entry.
Separate head and foot rules; top I additionally has a tall open-ended enclosing loop. The two occurrences were read independently.
Compact lower vertical, lateral and oblique parts; neither star nor plus is secure.
Open-bottom capital and raised hooked numeral 1; no prime or lower index.
Lowercase p, covered angular/intersecting sign and closed zero. The cancellation does not decide the sign.
Two opening hooks and two closing hooks around the Griffiths title; not guillemets.
Arabic 1 and 3 with two lower rules, independently of the two long cancellation strokes.
Final low loop favors e; a distinct i dot is not secure.

math_checks.result: There is no stated proof or computation to verify on this list page. No theorem, bibliographic identity or document count was externally checked.
A targeted visual comparison of the local oval and its transverse stroke confirms Theta. This is a glyph check, not a mathematical theorem check.
The crop was checked for superscript versus subscript and numeral versus prime: the hooked 1 with its foot is raised to the upper right of Omega.

The local sign was inspected for a second bar and crossing stroke. The deletion conceals enough of it that ne and > both remain. Mathematical expectations about characteristic were not used to select a reading.

The Roman groups visibly have one and two uprights; the Artin parenthesis reads 13 with two short rules. The two occurrences of 2 articles were read as source wording; no external count of articles was attempted.

workflow_feedback: Read the four required briefing/convention files and the assigned C/H/question/meta packet. The appended current-page C note about the Deligne question-mark alternative was read and covered by the existing local locus.

Whole image 1681 x 2138 viewed once for layout; half a 1681 x 1149 viewed once line by line; half b 1681 x 1149 viewed once line by line. Half b begins at whole-image y=989. Every agreement entry was checked from ink.

Twenty-one tightly targeted crops were made with out/scripts/crop.py and each viewed once. Several crops cover a neighboring cluster of unresolved marks in one line. No crop was repeated and no decided locus was re-viewed.
The complete reading.tex was saved before assembling this longer report. All output files and crop images were written only under the assigned R2 directory.
No OCR, web lookup, external edition, other page image, other reader file, root decision file, extra agent or optional TeX compilation was used.

Source geometry is encoded in one coordinate-based TikZ layout, with each list entry on its own source row. This preserves the two columns, the large blank above Illusie, the lower parenthetical note, and the long angled cancellations without redefining state macros.
The finite source resolution and covered low letter bodies limit several name and adjective readings. Those doubts remain in place; no contextual repair was made.

A text-only apparatus check confirmed all C/H difference quotations as exact substrings, checked every inventory transcribed value as yes, and matched the declared two divider strokes, two Papiers strikes, six schematic hatch diagonals plus terminal return, wavy underline, and isolated points to saved path commands. No additional image view or compilation was used.
